inline_comments.comment: The warning advice `"create a tsconfig.json that extends '${candidate}'"` can be incorrect when `candidate` is `tsconfig.app.json`. In Angular projects, `tsconfig.app.json` is a build-subset config that itself extends `tsconfig.json` — advising users to flip that relationship creates a potential circular `extends` chain and misleads Angular users about the conventional project structure. A safer, unconditional recommendation would be: `"Create a tsconfig.json in your project root"` without prescribing what it should extend.

The three-candidate fallback list (`tsconfig.json` → `tsconfig.base.json` → `tsconfig.app.json`) is hardcoded inline here, duplicating `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` from `code/renderers/react/src/componentManifest/utils.ts`. Because these live in different packages a direct import isn't trivial, but at minimum add a comment like `// Keep in sync with TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES in renderers/react/src/componentManifest/utils.ts`. Without it, a future contributor who adds a new candidate to `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` (e.g., `tsconfig.workspace.json`) will not know to update the Vite and Webpack loaders, silently leaving them out of sync.

Same duplication issue as in `react-docgen.ts`: the three-candidate fallback list is hardcoded without any reference to `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` in `utils.ts`. Add a comment pointing to that constant so future maintainers know to update all three locations when a new candidate is added.

The `tsconfig.app.json` fallback test only asserts `expect(logger.warn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.stringContaining('tsconfig.app.json'))`, but the analogous `tsconfig.base.json` test (around line 222–223) asserts both `'No tsconfig.json found'` and `'tsconfig.base.json'`. For consistency and stronger regression coverage, the `tsconfig.app.json` test should also assert `expect(logger.warn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.stringContaining('No tsconfig.json found'))`, ensuring the warning's introductory phrase is present regardless of which candidate is found.

The warning message `'No tsconfig.json (or tsconfig.base.json / tsconfig.app.json) found.'` is accurate when `configPath` is `undefined`, but this hardcodes the fallback candidate names in a second location — they already appear in `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` in `utils.ts`. If a new candidate is added to `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` in the future, this message string will become stale. Consider deriving the list from `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` (which is not currently exported) or extracting the message string alongside the constant.

general_comments.comment: The Vite (`react-docgen.ts`) and Webpack (`react-docgen-loader.ts`) loaders silently use fallback tsconfigs for path alias resolution without emitting any log output, while `findTsconfigPath` (used for docgen) explicitly warns when a fallback is used. A user in a monorepo with only `tsconfig.base.json` will see a warning for docgen but nothing for path aliases — which may lead them to believe path alias resolution is broken or simply inconsistent behavior across the two concerns. Either add analogous `logger.debug` messages in the loader fallback paths, or add inline comments explicitly documenting that the warning omission is intentional for alias resolution.

The `findTsconfigPath` function is wrapped with `cached`, which means the `logger.warn` side effect fires only once per unique `cwd` value. This is the right behavior (no warning spam), but it means if `invalidateCache()` is called mid-session (e.g., on an HMR reset), the warning will fire again on the next call. The tests call `invalidateCache()` in `beforeEach` which correctly isolates test cases, but the caching-of-warning behavior is not explicitly tested. Adding a test that calls `findTsconfigPath` twice with the same `cwd` (without invalidating) would confirm the warning fires exactly once, guarding against regressions in the `cached` integration.
